question: In Python, an if-statement is used to execute a block of code only if the specified condition is true.
The syntax for an if-statement in Python requires a colon at the end of the condition declaration.
An elif clause can be used to specify multiple conditions in an if-statement.
The default condition for an if-statement in Python is 'false' if not explicitly defined.
You can have multiple if-statements in a single block, but only one if-statement can be executed at a time.
In Python, using 'if x = 10:' will correctly check if x is equal to 10.
If a condition in an if-statement evaluates to false, the code block under the if will always run.
To check if a variable x is not equal to 5, you would write: if x != 5:.
In nested if-statements, you can place an if inside another if without any restrictions.
An if-statement can only evaluate expressions of data type integer.
